measuredNothing.why: Every timing in this task depends on being signed in as owner. Without a session the screen bounces to /login.html and paints no board.
measuredNothing.fieldsDeliberatelyNull: Everything below is null because it was NOT measured. None of these numbers were estimated, modelled or carried over from another role or another day.

whatWasMeasured.note: These are the only real numbers this workflow produced. They need no sign-in. They describe the SHELL's download weight, not the data fill.
whatWasMeasured.method: One GET per file from a headless Chromium request context against https://fundhub.ai, no session, no cache.
observations: Shell download weight is small: about 73 KB compressed. The shell is not the problem, which matches the Lighthouse score of 100.

Every file is served max-age=0, must-revalidate. A returning user still pays one round trip per file to be told the file has not changed. Six files = six round trips before the page can even start asking for data.
The uncompressed JavaScript the browser must parse and run is about 140 KB (shell.js 94 KB + data.js 32 KB + proxy-apply.js 14 KB), plus an 86 KB HTML file with the whole board script inlined.
whatWasMeasured.liveApiCaveat: A signed-out /api/health call takes about half a second round trip. That is one data point about API latency in general, NOT a measurement of the pipeline endpoint, which was never reachable without a session.

codeReadNotMeasured.warning: This is what the page source says it does. It is NOT measured and must not be reported as a timing. It is here so W3/W4 know what to look for the moment login works again.
codeReadNotMeasured.observation: On load the board calls loadRailCounts("R-01") and then load("R-01"). loadRailCounts fires one FHData.pipeline() request for each of the other 7 rails (funding_card_stacking, funding_altfin, optimization, inquiry_removal, ar_collections, affiliates_white_label, hiring) purely to fill the tab counters, while load() fetches the Sales board the user actually sees. That is 8 calls to GET /api/dashboard/pipeline on every page open. Whether they overlap or queue, and what each costs the owner, is exactly what this script was written to measure.

howToFinishThis: Wait for live writes to work again (POST /api/auth/login must stop returning 500).
It logs in once, caches the session, runs 3 cold loads in fresh contexts, 3 warm reloads, then a separate screenshot pass, and rewrites this file with real numbers.
W4 re-runs the same command with --label after --out <a different dir> to get the after numbers.
